answers.answer: Taking Oathkeeper during Act does not permit an immediate Usurper win. At the next Wake, the Exile's victory check occurs before the title flips, so they are not yet Usurper; the flip happens afterward. They can first win at the following Wake check, or at round 8 first if that endgame arrives while they still hold the title. If someone takes the title meanwhile, they cannot win as Usurper; taking it again resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Usurper victory: ‘next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake’; ‘Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper.’

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary win requires the Exile to have their true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and have at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck by all players combined. ‘Most’ for Conquest or Sanctuary means strictly more than every other player, so a tie does not qualify.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table; Visionary victory: ‘at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck by all players combined’ and ‘strictly more than every other player, no ties.’

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll. A Citizen who meets their Successor goal wins alone instead of the Chancellor if the roll ends the game. No other round-end die roll is specified.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Stable regime: ‘ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7’; ‘6 / 5–6 / 3–6’; ‘An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.’

answers.answer: Round 8 ends automatically. Check: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins; a qualified Citizen Successor wins alone instead of Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions ordered Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, Chancellor unless a qualified Successor applies. An Exile who is merely Oathkeeper does not prevent the fallback Empire win. A Successor goal alone never ends the game; it is resolved whenever Chancellor would win.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → War exhaustion: ‘Check in this exact priority’ followed by the four listed outcomes; ‘Holding Successor goal never ends game on its own.’

answers.answer: Citizen Successor goals: under Supremacy, hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; under People, hold Darkest Secret; under Protection, hold People's Favor; under Devotion, hold the Grand Scepter. Citizens and Chancellor cannot win through a true Vision or as Usurper.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table, ‘Citizen Successor goal’; Visionary victory: ‘Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.’

answers.answer: At Wake, the holder chooses to add 1 favor from their board to People's Favor or return 1 favor from it to the least-full suit bank, choosing among ties. They may not remove its last favor: at 1 they must add if able, and if unable nothing happens. On the Mob side, repeat the choice once. After those choices, check whether it has 6 or more favor and flip it to Mob if so. Becoming Mob at this final check does not trigger an extra payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake: ‘Never remove its last favor’; ‘If banner is already Mob-side, repeat this choice once’; ‘Afterwards, if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob.’

answers.answer: Rest in order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply (Exile/Chancellor based on their warbands remaining in personal bank, Citizen to the exact Chancellor marker space); save each unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent point, capped at leftmost (7 Supply); then optionally use Rest powers once each in chosen order. The refresh thresholds are Chancellor 18+ = 6, 11–17 = 5, 4–10 = 4, 0–3 = 3; Exile 9+ = 6, 4–8 = 5, 0–3 = 4. Citizen refresh is not based on counting purple warbands.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Rest: five ordered steps; Citizen refreshes to ‘exact Chancellor marker space’; ‘Save remaining unspent Supply… capped at leftmost (7 Supply).’

answers.answer: Search costs 2 Supply from your region discard pile; world-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, or 4 at 3–5. Darkest Secret replaces world-deck cost with 2, while other modifiers still apply. Choose one source only. Draw up to 3 (fewer if source runs out, world Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it); cannot voluntarily stop early. From the world deck, draw one at a time; if a Vision appears, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision from a discard pile does not stop drawing or advance the track.
answers.evidence: Actions → Search: source costs and ‘draw one at a time’; world-deck Vision ‘stop immediately and increase Visions Drawn by 1’; discard Vision ‘does not stop drawing or advance the track.’

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle, never the same-region pile. Cards from hand/advisers use the pawn's region to determine the next pile. If discarding a card at a remote site in another region, use the card's region for that cycle instead. Favor on a discarded card returns immediately to its matching bank; secrets on it go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Actions → Discard destinations: ‘When discarding a card at a site in another region, apply that cycle to the card’s region instead of your pawn’s’; resource destinations follow.

answers.answer: Advisers are limited to 3 total, faceup and facedown. Before going over the limit, discard an adviser subject to locks; if an incoming card changes the limit, check using the new limit before playing and use the lowest limit if several apply. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card—including site-only cards and Visions—can be held facedown. Later, play a facedown adviser faceup to a legal destination or discard it as a minor action; a faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when another rule permits or requires it. An Exile may play a true Vision faceup into the separate Revealed Vision slot, replacing and discarding the old revealed Vision; it is not an adviser. Chancellor/Citizens may keep a true Vision facedown but cannot reveal it.
answers.evidence: Actions → Search, Adviser and True Vision bullets; Minor actions: ‘Play or discard a facedown adviser’; true Vision ‘replacing and discarding old revealed Vision.’

answers.answer: Both actions cost 1 Supply and require an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site; it must have no favor or secrets already. Muster places 1 favor on it and gains 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board (Citizens gain purple). Trade either puts 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank, or puts 2 favor on it to gain 1 secret from the shared bank per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers do not match. With no matching faceup advisers, the second Trade option gains zero secrets, but its 2 favor cost remains. Relics and ruins are ineligible; ruling a remote site does not permit these actions there. Finite favor/warband supply limits gains; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Actions → Muster / Trade: empty card at pawn's site; ‘With no matching advisers gain zero secrets’; ‘Costs remain payable even if a gain is reduced to zero.’

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank, by paying any amount of its resource strictly greater than its current amount. For People's Favor, put the new favor on it and distribute the old favor one at a time to suit banks, starting at any bank and proceeding away from the world deck in printed bank order, wrapping as needed; do not return it to the previous holder, and flip Mob to normal. No seizure penalty applies to Recover. For Darkest Secret, put paid secrets on it; new holder takes 1 old secret and previous holder gets the remainder. If recovering it from yourself, all old secrets return to you; from shared bank, the remainder stays there.
answers.evidence: Actions → Recover: ‘strictly greater’; People's Favor and Darkest Secret bullets specify old-resource distribution and self/shared-bank exceptions.

answers.answer: To recover Darkest Secret from another player, their pawn's site must contain at least one suited card whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. One such card is enough even if other cards match. If the holder has no faceup advisers but has a suited card at the site, it is recoverable (the corrected errata rule). An empty site protects it, as does a ruin-only site: neither supplies a suited card. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. Self-recovery and recovery from the shared bank ignore this protection.
answers.evidence: Recover → Darkest Secret protection: ‘at least one suited card…whose suit matches none’; ‘Empty sites and ruin-only sites protect it’; no-faceup-adviser case is ‘recoverable.’

answers.answer: Campaign costs 2 Supply. Choose another player who rules your site or whose pawn is there; if nobody rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, it must be targeted. You may also target any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map, each adding 1 defense die. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may instead/additionally target their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to resources on them), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice); a co-located relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. If a Citizen attacks Chancellor/another Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; if Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2: defender criteria, local target requirement, remote sites, and co-located relic/banner/pawn targets.

answers.answer: Attacker chooses up to one attack die per warband in their attacking board force. Defender rolls defense dice; each shield counts, and each double-symbol doubles shields (multipliers stack), then add defending warbands at targeted sites, defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or any target, and 1 per targeted bandit site. Doubles do not multiply warbands. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords plus one sword per pair of hollow swords; a leftover hollow sword counts zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but must sacrifice exactly enough to win and cannot sacrifice excess. The attacker wins only if attack strictly exceeds defense; a tie is a defender win.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4–5: attack dice capped by force; shield doubling; skulls kill; hollow swords pair; tie or lower means defender wins; sacrifice exactly enough.

answers.answer: On attacker victory, first the defender kills half of warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board; resolve defeated plan effects. Then attacker may put any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands on targeted sites. Zero leaves a site to bandits unless a power says otherwise. Take all targeted relics and banners. Any banner seized other than by Recover has 2 resources burned, to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, attacker may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and independently may burn half the defender's board favor rounded down. Respect travel restrictions and Shrouded Wood's ruler choice. Finish victorious attacker battle-plan effects and discard plans marked ‘At end, discard.’ If attacker loses, attacker kills half remaining force rounded down, leaves survivors on board, and defender skips attacker targets; resolve defender's victorious effects. The transfer of Supremacy title happens at Campaign end, not during temporary loss of site rule.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8: defeat casualties before targets; ‘any number, including zero’; seizure penalty; forced travel/favor; order of plan effects.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally; other non-attacking Citizens may join with defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker site or any target. The defending side activates all relevant modifiers and shares powers as one side, but ‘your site/your board’ remain each user's own. Allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at attacker site or a target. Allies can use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not others' advisers; each shared plan can be used once total by one user, who pays. The declared defender chooses order, timing, priority, and plan use if Allies disagree. Chancellor chooses Imperial defending casualties; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while Citizen board warbands stay on those boards. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make every Citizen non-Imperial. When a Citizen attacks another Imperial player, that attacker is non-Imperial for that Campaign; when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that defender is non-Imperial. Those specified participants lose that status temporarily for the Campaign.
answers.evidence: Campaign → Imperial defense bullets; step 1 and final Imperial-defense bullet specify temporary non-Imperial status.

answers.answer: Base Travel costs before modifiers are: Cradle→Cradle 1, Cradle→Provinces 2, Cradle→Hinterland 4; Provinces→Cradle 2, Provinces→Provinces 2, Provinces→Hinterland 2; Hinterland→Cradle 4, Hinterland→Provinces 2, Hinterland→Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. Reveal a facedown destination and place its printed favor/secrets from shared bank and its printed relics facedown from the relic deck. Pay fixed-number cost first, then apply other increases/decreases. Any applicable ‘spend no Supply’ free-Travel power is the final override and reduces the payment to zero even if another power increased it; this applies to all Travel including banishment. Site entry restrictions remain unless ignored by a power.
answers.evidence: Actions → Travel: table of costs; reveal/stock destination; ‘fixed-number cost first’; ‘Free Travel is the final override.’

answers.answer: The Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, or exile another Citizen, but cannot use Scepter powers on the turn they took it. A Citizenship offer likewise cannot be made the turn the current holder took the Scepter. The offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, the Exile flips to Citizen and replaces all their board and map warbands with purple (if short, the new Citizen chooses removals/replacements), discards a revealed Vision, flips their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if accepting on their own turn, and refreshes to full leftmost Supply. They exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gets the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers use the same status conversion without a negotiated offer, required Scepter offer, Reliquary gift, or invented exchange; only an actual Reliquary relic removal uncovers its modifier.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play → Grand Scepter / Offer / Acceptance / Forced Citizenship paragraphs.

answers.answer: Chronicle Oath choice: if the winner won by Vision alone, next Oath matches that Vision; otherwise—including multiple victory methods—choose any Oath except the current one, and save the goal. For free Chronicle Citizenship, ignore ordinary offer requirements: no Reliquary relic, resource payment, or Scepter permission is needed. If winner is Exile, flip all Citizen boards, even boxed ones, to Exile, then they may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile must flip to Citizen and replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband; winner cannot offer themself. Rebuild world deck by shuffling all denizens remaining in play (excluding cards retained at sites, Archive, and Dispossessed); make top stack 10 denizens + 2 random Visions (12 cards), middle stack 15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), and remaining denizens below. Thus the top stack is 12 cards, not 14: the Chronicle aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ is explicitly identified as incorrect.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle steps 1–2 and 9: new Oath and turnover; step 9 specifies ‘10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12’ and says the aid's 12-denizen instruction is incorrect.
